capitals.note: 'His capital was the Gandharan city of Taxila' (Gondophares page); 'The city of Taxila is thought to have been a capital of the Indo-Parthians' (Indo-Parthian page). After the Kushans began absorbing 'the northern Indian part' no page names a seat for the Sakastan remnant.

keyframe_review.note: 487,414 km2 (66.1-73.6E, 22.9-34.4N). The page dates the kingdom to 19/20 CE ('founded in 19/20', Gondophares 'ruling from 19 to 46'; infobox c. 19), 18 years after Cliopatria's first Indo-Parthian shape. Senior would date Gondophares before 1 CE (Apostle Thomas passage), but that is one view and the page's own dates are 19/20.

Cliopatria's shape holds Punjab, Sindh and the Kabul valley but not Seistan or Arachosia, which are added. Used from 19/20 to 42.

The cells are Cliopatria's Sistan shape of 121,799 km2 (listed under the Indo-Scythians in 91..282); Turan, which the Sakastan page pairs with Sakastan, is not placed. The Sakastan page says Parthian satraps and the Suren ruled it before Gondophares and the Sasanian province was formed around 240.

ledger.note: 19 CE: Gondophares declares independence in Drangiana. 'The kingdom was founded in 19/20 when the governor of Drangiana' declared independence from Parthia; the Gondophares page has him 'ruling from 19 to 46'. Infobox 'c. 19 - 46'.

region.text: Arachosia, Sindh, Punjab and the Kabul valley (Cliopatria's Indo-Parthian shape plus Arachosia)

ledger.note: c. 20 CE: Gondophares takes the Kabul valley, Punjab and Sindh. 'Gondophares became the ruler of areas comprising Arachosia, Seistan, Sindh, Punjab, and the Kabul valley', 'perhaps after the death of the important ruler Azes'; Gondophares page: he 'took over the Kabul valley and the Punjab and Sindh region area from the Scythian king Azes' and 'Indo-Scythian vassal rulers reportedly switched allegiance'. The same page also says 'Around 20–10 BC, he made conquests in the former Indo-Scythian kingdom, perhaps after the death of the important ruler Azes', which conflicts with its 'founded in 19/20'; 20 CE follows the founding date and the infobox (confidence lowered to 1 by the sa-02-b reviewer).

region.text: the northern Indian part: Gandhara, Taxila and the Kabul valley

ledger.note: c. 50 CE: the Kushans begin absorbing the north. 'From the middle of the 1st century AD the Kushans under Kujula Kadphises began absorbing the northern Indian part of the kingdom'; Hou Hanshu (Kushan page): Kujula 'invaded Anxi (Indo-Parthia), and took the Gaofu (Kabul) region' and 'defeated the whole of the kingdoms of Puda (Paktiya) and Jibin (Kapisha and Gandhara)'. The absorption is gradual; 50 is the page's 'middle of the century'.

ledger.note: c. 90 CE: Punjab and Sindh pass to the Kushans. Cliopatria's Indian shape ends in 90; the Kushan page has Vima Takto (c. 80-127) 'expanded the Kushan Empire into the northwest of South Asia' and 'defeated Tianzhu (North-western India) and installed Generals'. No page dates the last Indo-Parthian loss.

c. 226 CE: the Sasanians take Sakastan. 'They managed to retain control of Sakastan, until its conquest by the Sasanian Empire in c. 224/5'; 'The Kingdoms of Turan and Sakastan ended when they submitted to the Sasanian ruler Ardeshir I circa 230 CE'. The infobox gives 226.

wars.outcome: Gondophares 'took over the Kabul valley and the Punjab and Sindh region area from the Scythian king Azes'; Indo-Scythian vassals switched allegiance. His holdings did not pass eastern Punjab.
wars.note: The page gives no campaign and no battle; the years are the reign (19-46).

wars.name: Kushan absorption of the Indo-Parthian north

zones.text: the northern Indian part: Gandhara, Taxila and the Kabul valley

wars.outcome: The Kushans under Kujula Kadphises 'began absorbing the northern Indian part of the kingdom' from the middle of the 1st century; the Indo-Parthians refocused on Turan and Sakastan.
wars.note: The Indo-Scythians page puts the Kushan regain of north-western India at c. 75 CE; Vima Takto (c. 80-127) is the Kushan page's conqueror of north-west India. The end year 90 is Cliopatria's.

wars.name: Sasanian conquest of Sakastan
wars.outcome: Sakastan conquered c. 224/5; 'the Kingdoms of Turan and Sakastan ended when they submitted to Ardeshir I circa 230 CE'.
wars.note: Ardashir I (r. 224-242) rebuilt Zrang as the provincial capital (Sakastan page); the province was formed around 240 under Shapur I.

certainty.note: Known from coins, a few inscriptions and Greek and Chinese lines; no frontier is dated or surveyed. The Sakastan core is better attested than the Indian lands.

notes:
Cliopatria row Indo-Parthians 1..90, 5 shapes. Five pages opened (budget 5). No page gives an area, so no ratio.

Departures from Cliopatria: (1) start 19, not 1 (page: 'founded in 19/20'); (2) end 226, not 90: the page has the kingdom keep Sakastan to c. 224/5 (infobox 226), so a new Sistan keyframe 91..226 uses Cliopatria's Indo-Scythian 91 cells; (3) Seistan and Arachosia added to the Indian shape; (4) the northern Indian part dropped from 50, Punjab and Sindh from 90.

Not settled: (a) the pages disagree on when the Kushans took the Indian lands (mid-1st century 'began'; c. 75 CE in the Indo-Scythians page; Vima Takto after 80; Cliopatria 90). (b) Senior's earlier dating of Gondophares (before 1 CE) is mentioned on the Indo-Parthian page. (c) Turan (Makran/Kalat) is paired with Sakastan on the page but has no placed region. (d) Cliopatria carves this shape out of the Indo-Scythian row from 1 CE (the Indo-Scythian area falls by 488,383 km2, this shape being 487,414); the indo-scythians dossier gives the core back to the Indo-Scythians until 19. (e) Sakastan 100 BC-19 CE (Parthian satraps, the Suren) belongs to the parthian-empire dossier (me-06). Rulers omitted: only Gondophares (c. 19-46) is dated; Sarpedones, Abdagases, Orthagnes, Ubouzanes and Pacores have no years.
The Gondophares I page was not found under that title (retry with 'Gondophares' worked); the sources list the working URL.
